clue.text: Number harbouring resistance talk about company in military-style fashion

indicators.note: a number harbouring something holds it within, so the R goes inside

parts.note: ten is a number
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

indicators.note: talk placed about company surrounds it, so the CO goes inside

parts.note: a chat is a talk

explanation.surface: A fashion story about a military look, with a stray number, resistance and company chat.
explanation.definitionFit: A trench coat is a belted raincoat first worn by officers in the trenches, now a fashion staple with military styling.

clue.text: Having gone topless, characters felt line should be banter

indicators.note: going topless means losing the top, the first letter of a down entry's word

parts.note: Braille characters are read by feeling raised dots
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: Someone discusses whether letters felt by the fingers should be read as playful teasing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having gone topless' removes the first letter of BRAILLE, leaving RAILLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Raillery is good-humoured teasing, the same thing as friendly banter.

clue.text: Born to want, found wanting

indicators.note: a word found wanting is short of something, here its last letter

parts.note: to need something is to want it

explanation.surface: A slogan about a person born into need and judged inadequate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found wanting' cuts the final D from NEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Nee, from French, introduces a woman's maiden name: born with that surname.

clue.text: Runs in preliminary race, showing spirit

indicators.note: runs put in the race sit inside it

parts.note: a heat is a qualifying race before a final
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An athlete shows grit by running in a qualifying race.
explanation.definitionFit: Heart means courage or fighting spirit, as in a player who shows plenty of heart.

clue.text: Folding payment up, friend crossing channel

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a giro is a payment made by bank transfer or a benefit cheque
ami is French for friend, the word on the other side of the English Channel

explanation.surface: Money is sent off while a friend crosses the Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns GIRO into ORIG; the Channel here is the English Channel, beyond which a friend is French AMI.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese art of paper folding, so folding is a fair loose definition.

clue.text: "I want a skyscraper built by tomorrow" — you'll be lucky!

definitions.text: "I want a skyscraper built by tomorrow" — you'll be lucky!

parts.words: "I want a skyscraper built by tomorrow" — you'll be lucky!
parts.note: the demand is an instruction for something high to be made, and also an unreasonable request nobody could meet

explanation.surface: An impossible demand to a builder is met with a scoffing reply.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall order is an unreasonably difficult demand, and literally a commission for a tall building.

clue.text: Neighbour's coming round — blow it!

indicators.note: turning round means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to abut is to neighbour, to lie next to

explanation.surface: Annoyance as the neighbour turns up uninvited: blow it!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow it!' looks like an exclamation of annoyance, but it defines a brass instrument one blows.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuba is a large brass instrument played by blowing, something you blow.

clue.text: Edit Marxist play? I know my stuff

indicators.note: to play with letters is to rearrange them freely

explanation.surface: A director proposes editing a Marxist drama, boasting of expertise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' looks like a noun, a drama, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxidermist stuffs dead animals, so is one who knows about stuffing, punning on knowing one's stuff.

clue.text: Keen to invest money in major league INCE

clue.text: Great minds fired time and time again, one succeeding

indicators.note: succeeding means coming after, so this piece follows the rest

parts.note: lit means set alight, fired
an era is a span of time
T is the standard abbreviation for time
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Clever people are inspired again and again, each following the last.
explanation.definitionFit: The literati are learned, intellectual people, the great minds of a society.

clue.text: Neglect the non-clerical clutching cross

indicators.note: something clutching another holds it inside

parts.note: the laity are people who are not clergy
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: Ordinary churchgoers, holding a crucifix, are accused of slackness.
explanation.definitionFit: Laxity is slackness or carelessness, a form of neglect.

clue.text: Private to wind up sergeant, ultimately

parts.note: to wind up a meeting is to close it

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A private soldier sets out to annoy his sergeant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' and 'sergeant' suggest army ranks and 'wind up' teasing; Private is the adjective, as in a closet admirer.
explanation.definitionFit: Closet as an adjective means secret or hidden, as in a closet fan, so private.

clue.text: 12 E major enters minor — that must be NEAT brilliant

clue.text: Escaping Roman seven, go and set off

indicators.note: letters set off are sent in a new direction, rearranged

parts.note: VII is seven in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A Roman legion of seven men decides to go and depart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set off' rearranges VII plus GO and AND into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Avoiding means escaping or evading, as in avoiding capture.

clue.text: Controller taking command around group, right at home

indicators.note: the command is placed around the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: an order is a command
a gang is a group
in means at home

explanation.surface: A leader issues orders to a group while staying home.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'deal with the organ grinder, not the monkey' makes the street musician the one really in control.
explanation.definitionFit: In the saying about the organ grinder and his monkey, the grinder is the one in charge, a controller.

clue.text: Volunteer to inject iodine into arm: I gape as it circulates

indicators.note: to inject one thing into another puts it inside
into says where the iodine goes, inside the arm

parts.note: a gun is an arm, a weapon
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

indicators.note: something circulating moves around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A test subject gapes as iodine is injected into an arm and spreads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arm' suggests a limb but is a weapon; 'circulates' rearranges I GAPE into EAPIG.
explanation.definitionFit: A guinea pig is someone who volunteers to be experimented on, a test subject.

clue.text: Shiny silver sweet wrappers etc.

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
discarded sweet wrappers and the like are litter

explanation.surface: Shiny silver wrappers from sweets are scattered around.
explanation.definitionFit: Aglitter means glittering, sparkling, so shiny.

clue.text: Holds to restrict fighter showing guts

indicators.note: holds restricting the fighter close round it

parts.note: to cling is to hold tightly
a hitter is a fighter, a puncher

explanation.surface: A wrestler restricts a boxer with holds, showing grit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guts' looks like courage, the boxing scene's quality, but it is the literal sense: pig intestines.
explanation.definitionFit: Chitterlings are the small intestines of a pig cooked as food, literally guts.

clue.text: Lot more quivering brings such an effect

indicators.note: quivering letters shake into a new order

explanation.surface: A lot more trembling produces exactly that musical effect.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the clue: the effect is that of quivering.
explanation.definitionFit: Tremolo is a musical effect of rapid repetition or wavering, a quivering sound.

clue.text: Copper, unusual poison

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
rare means unusual

explanation.surface: A policeman uncovers an unusual poisoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' reads as a policeman but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Curare is a plant poison used on arrow tips in South America.

clue.text: Tough to contain Kent's English hot shot

indicators.note: the tough holds the other piece within it

parts.note: a bully is a tough, a thug
Kent is a county in the south-east of England, SE

explanation.surface: A tough guy from Kent proves a sharp marksman.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is an English county in the South East, so SE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullseye is a direct hit at the centre of the target, a crack shot.

clue.text: All but dead, going through country

indicators.note: all but means everything except the last letter

parts.note: late means dead, as in the late king
via means going through, by way of

explanation.surface: A traveller, nearly dead, passes through a land.
explanation.definitionFit: Latvia is a Baltic country in north-eastern Europe.

clue.text: Religious sect practically raised on money

indicators.note: in a down entry raised means read upwards, backwards
practically means almost, the word less its last letter

parts.note: a cult is a religious sect
re means on, concerning

explanation.surface: A religious sect has been practically built on money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'practically' cuts CULT to CUL, and 'raised' turns that into LUC.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is money, especially gained dishonestly, as in filthy lucre.

clue.text: Psychologically problematic conclusion to phone call?

definitions.meaning: a neurosis or fixation, something one is troubled by
the act of putting the receiver down to end a call

explanation.definitionFit: A hang-up is a neurotic fixation, and also the ending of a call by putting the phone down.

clue.text: Kiss model, also cute

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so these letters are moulded into new order

explanation.surface: A fashion model, cute as well, gets a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' looks like a noun but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To osculate is a formal or jocular word for to kiss.

clue.text: Heavy type endlessly climbing, shot up

indicators.note: in a down entry climbing means the letters are read upwards
endlessly means without the final letter

parts.note: bold type is heavy type in printing

explanation.surface: A heavy fellow keeps climbing, then is shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts BOLD to BOL; 'climbing' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: A lob is a shot hit high into the air, as in tennis.

clue.text: Following figure turns around itself

indicators.note: the reversed figure goes around the other piece
a figure that turns is read backwards

parts.note: ten is a figure, a number
the figure ten is X in Roman numerals, so it stands for itself

explanation.surface: A figure revolves around its own centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'itself' refers back to the figure ten, written as Roman X; 'turns' makes NET.
explanation.definitionFit: Next means following, coming immediately after.

clue.text: See albatross progress one way after extra turns

indicators.note: after puts this piece behind the extra

parts.note: to go on is to progress

indicators.note: turns means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a bye is an extra in cricket, a run not scored off the bat
I is the Roman numeral one
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A dictionary cross-reference sends you to albatross while a game goes on with extras.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a dictionary's cross-reference. A bye is a cricket run scored without the bat touching the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Gooney bird is a sailors' name for the albatross.
